metaTitle: Flooring Installers in Ontario: A Buyer's Guide
metaDescription: What to check before hiring a flooring installer in Ontario, from subfloor prep and moisture testing to material costs and questions worth asking.
intro: Flooring installation depends as much on what is underneath as what you see on top, and skipping subfloor prep is one of the most common causes of early failure. Different materials also carry different moisture tolerances, especially in basements and over concrete, so the right prep steps change depending on what you choose.
whatToLookFor: A subfloor inspection and levelling plan before installation
Moisture testing for concrete slabs, especially in basements
Direct, hands-on experience with the specific material you're choosing, such as hardwood, LVP, tile or carpet
Acclimation time built in for wood and engineered products
Clear transition and trim details between rooms and flooring types
typicalCostNotes: Flooring costs can range considerably by material, from budget-friendly laminate and carpet to solid hardwood and natural stone tile, with labour also shifting based on subfloor condition and how much old flooring needs removal. Uneven subfloors or moisture issues found during removal can add cost once the quote is already in place, and stairs or intricate transitions often carry their own separate pricing. Ask whether subfloor prep and old flooring disposal are included or billed separately.
questionsToAsk: Have you checked the subfloor condition and levelness?
Will you test for moisture before installing over concrete?
How long does this material need to acclimate before install?
Is removal and disposal of the old flooring included?
What warranty applies to materials versus your installation labour?
redFlags: No subfloor inspection before quoting the job
Installing wood or laminate with no acclimation period
Vague pricing that doesn't separate material from labour
